verdict: Red 7/10 REJECT, blue 8/10 SUSTAINED with two reductions and one overreach corrected - concordant on the verdict, with blue notably making the record MORE accurate in both directions rather than simply ratifying the prosecution. The triage was honest that CWH does not qualify as damage-absent: every metric the cohort narrative predicts would deteriorate has deteriorated on the company's own numbers within the prior two weeks. Q2-26, reported 2026-07-29: same-store new vehicle units -16.3%, new gross margin 10.9% (down 286bps), used gross margin 16.5% (down 397bps), total gross profit -9.1%, adjusted EBITDA $112.1M (down 21.2%), and the FY26 adjusted-EBITDA guide cut from $275-325M to $230-270M against an industry new-retail guide cut from 325-350k to 290-310k units. The dividend was already suspended on 2026-02-25 alongside an FY25 net loss attributable of $89.8M. The one counter-datum - same-store USED units +5.2% on 19,882 units - is volume bought with margin, so it refutes 'no traffic', not 'no earnings'. The sizing fork the court actually adjudicated is solvency-versus-trough-option, and it is arithmetic. At $6.34 with roughly 103.72M economic units, the $658M cap plus $1.31B of net debt gives an EV of about $1.97B, or 7.9x the midpoint of the freshly-cut FY26 guide - not trough-cheap. Red's strongest kill is that every number supporting the convex-starter tail is either the smallest available basis or unverified, while every confirmed number feeds the zero. The net-debt basis is the clearest instance: $1,377.5M of long-term debt net plus $124.1M of finance leases less $224.1M of cash gives roughly $1.28B, which is close to the triage's figure - but it EXCLUDES $874.7M of operating-lease liabilities (blue corrected red here; red cited only the $810.0M noncurrent portion) and $1,324.2M of floor plan. The fixed-obligation stack is about $3.6B, not $1.31B, and the '2.5-3x on normalization' tail is computed against the smallest of those bases. Blue sustained and strengthened this. Second, the deleveraging is one-shot. The $222.3M net-debt reduction the triage cited came from inventory liquidation - new units down about 17% and used down 18% - which is working capital, not earnings; blue verified YTD operating cash flow of +$333M against six-month net income of about $70M, confirming the bulk is a working-capital release. Blue's fair reduction: $333M is real cash and the aging profile genuinely improved (prior-model-year exposure cut from 6% to 1%), so red's 'nothing but liquidation' overreads the character even though the character is right. Third, and this is where blue materially corrected the record on BOTH sides: red argued the bull's $400M normalization EBITDA 'exceeds any non-COVID year (FY19 approximately $290M)'. Blue pulled the primary reconciliations and found red simply wrong - FY2017 adjusted EBITDA was $394.2M, so $400M is roughly the 2017 peak on a store base about 40% larger, which is not fantasy. But the same pull produced FY2019 at $166.0M, which sits BELOW the triage's own $180M bear case. The correction cuts both ways and makes the distribution wider than either prior document had it. Blue's most important new finding is bull-direction and goes to the actual insolvency channel: the floor-plan syndicate RAISED capacity from $1.85B to $2.15B, leaving roughly $825M of nominal headroom against the $1,324.2M balance. Lender behavior on the channel that would actually force a liquidity event currently points AWAY from stress, so red's 'every confirmed number feeds the zero' overreaches - and blue said so. Against that, blue widened red's springing-maturity finding: the revolver matures 2028-03-03 OR 91 days before the FreedomRoads floor-plan maturity, whichever comes first - a second springing linkage neither the triage nor red had, and the operative notes-spring text is still unread. The refi question at roughly 5.2x trough leverage against a $1.4B term loan maturing 2028 remains the whole equity, and the documents that discriminate the tails - the 10-Q liquidity note, floor-plan availability and curtailment terms, covenant headroom, and the credit-agreement springing text - were never read behind an environment-wide EDGAR 403. On doctrine: this is a business-risk and timing kill. Not damage-absent, not trough-cheap at 7.9x a twice-cut guide, catalyst roughly 2.5 months out, and the tape 15.6% off a recent low with falling-knife discipline applying. But blue is right that the correct posture is watch-with-defined-triggers rather than red's near-terminal framing - the floor-plan capacity raise is genuine evidence against the fast-collapse branch, and the FY2017 precedent means the upside tail is not a fabrication.
reopen_gates: PRIMARY read of the Q2-26 10-Q liquidity note and the credit agreement once EDGAR access is restored - floor-plan AVAILABILITY and curtailment schedule, covenant headroom, real-estate collateral (specifically how much is already sale-leased-back), and the operative springing-maturity text for the senior secured notes. This is the gate: neither bench read a single filing, and these are the documents that discriminate a 2.5-3x from a zero.
